claim: L9 (LFP-primary analysis spec): Granger causality and phase-slope index across area x layer node pairs, per band, stim vs omission, both directions reported separately, SNR-matched subsampling control per spec's own caution.
implementation: context/figures/L9_directed_lfp_lfp_influence/L9_directed_lfp_lfp_influence.py. Reuses jnwb.connectivity.granger_spectral (Geweke frequency-resolved GC, already-built n_surrogates trial-shuffle null used AS omission-signal S10's within-session null, not rebuilt) and jnwb.connectivity.phase_slope_index (PSI) verbatim. One representative channel per (area,layer) node, inheriting L8's node-key-collision fix from the start. SNR-matched subsampling: both conditions subsampled (seeded, without replacement, X/Y pairing preserved) to min(n_trials_stim, n_trials_omission) before either condition's GC/PSI is computed -- implements the spec's own explicit 'Caution: GC is sensitive to differing SNR between conditions... include an SNR-matched subsampling control' literally.
self_test: Synthetic bivariate AR system, X drives Y with a 2-sample lag (Y[t]+=0.6*X[t-2]), no reverse path: GC net recovered +0.600 (want>0) -- PASS. PSI recovered +1.17 (want>0, X leads Y) -- PASS. Independent AR(1) control: GC net~0.000, well below driven system's magnitude -- PASS. SNR-matched subsampling equalizes (50,30) trial counts to (30,30) while preserving X/Y trial pairing within each condition -- PASS. Determinism also PASS.
bug_found_and_fixed: Pseudoreplication in the cross-session CI aggregation: a single session can contribute MULTIPLE node-pair instances to the same (area,layer) identity when one session records the same area on two different probes (confirmed: sub-V182o_ses-260702 records FEF on probes A and B, so identity 'FEFsup-FEFdeep' got 3 pair instances from that ONE session). The first aggregation pass bootstrapped raw pair instances directly, letting one session count as up to 3 'sessions' in the CI (confirmed: FEFsup-FEFdeep showed n_sessions=5 from only 3 real sessions) -- exactly the channel-vs-session inflation omission-statistics warns against, at the pair-instance level. Fixed by averaging a session's own pair instances to ONE point estimate per session before bootstrapping over genuine session replicates. The raw per-session-per-pair GC/PSI values (stats['sessions'] tree) were correct all along and were NOT recomputed -- only the pairs_across_sessions aggregation was reapplied against the already-computed real-data output, avoiding a ~19-minute GC recomputation. Post-fix, max n_sessions across all 270 pair identities is correctly capped at 3.

real_run.runtime: 19m14s (90 pair-conditions x 5 bands x 2 directions x 50 surrogates for GC, plus PSI per pair-condition)
real_run.diagnostics: Zero GC or PSI diagnostic warnings across all 90 computed pair-conditions (spectral_radius<1 throughout, no non-stationarity flags) -- VAR fits numerically well-behaved.
real_run.finding_1: FEFsup-FEFdeep (same-probe, adjacent depth) is the ONLY pair with a genuine 3-session replicate and a CI excluding zero: theta net=-0.174 [-0.286,-0.099] stim, -0.158 [-0.238,-0.016] omission -- consistent direction (FEFdeep Granger-causes FEFsup more than reverse) across all 3 sessions.
real_run.finding_1_caveat: This is exactly the pair type L6/L7/L8 all independently flag as volume-conduction-dominated (near-1 coherence, near-zero imaginary coherency, near-1 trial-power correlation for same-probe adjacent-depth pairs). SNR-matched trial-count subsampling addresses unequal trial counts between conditions but NOT within-pair channel-SNR asymmetry, a known route to spurious GC directional asymmetry between two channels of a shared/mixed field. Stated explicitly in the README -- this finding must not be read as feedforward/feedback evidence without that caveat.
real_run.finding_2: The two largest-magnitude net asymmetries (PFCsup-PFCdeep, MSTsup-MSTdeep) are NOT robust: PFCsup-PFCdeep has n_sessions=2 with a CI crossing zero widely (e.g. alpha stim -0.294 [-0.918,+0.331]); MSTsup-MSTdeep is a single-session point estimate with a degenerate (non-informative) CI, stated explicitly via the stats JSON's ci_note field.
real_run.finding_3: No systematic alpha/beta-omission vs gamma-stim asymmetry pattern (the spec's predicted top-down feedback/feedforward signature) is visible across cross-area (non-same-probe) pairs in this small single-subject (V182o), 3-session sample -- reported plainly, neither spun into a positive claim nor into a dramatized null.
real_run.reported_honestly: All findings reported descriptively per the spec's own 'do not conclude' instruction (0.8) and CLAUDE.md tripwire 10.

not_yet_done: granger_spectral's p_surrogate is broadband-derived and shared identically across all bands within one call (a documented limitation of the underlying jnwb function, not something this script can fix without changing that function) -- PSI's per-band jackknife z is the genuinely per-band significance proxy reported alongside it. Single representative channel per node, not channel-resolved or node-averaged. Only 3 sessions, single subject (V182o) -- not planned, stated as a limitation. No formal correction across the 270 pair-identity x band x condition family (would need an FDR pass akin to L7's, not built here given the exploratory/descriptive framing already carried by the CI-not-p-value reporting).
